text:
Sam: heads-up — noticed a p95 latency spike on /generate in the A100 pool around 03:12 UTC. perf-bot posted an alert. I did a quick profile: KV cache hit-rate drops ~30% when short+long requests mix, which is triggering kernel-selector fallbacks and a bunch of extra scanning. Thinking: introduce a 'token_silo' softcap per-accelerator to isolate long-token requests into dedicated micro-slots so we reduce KV fragmentation and kernel thrash. Initial suggested softcaps: A100=48000, H100=64000, A10=18000, L4=10000, T4=6000. Thoughts?

perf-bot: alert: p95 latency 220ms -> 420ms; kernel-fallback-rate +3.2%; affected pool: a100-mixed-pack; window: 03:09-03:16 UTC.

Maria: quick profiler dump i grabbed after the spike — small excerpt:
```
profiler://kernel_selector.log
A100: fallback_count 342 -> 977 (mix short<64 + long>512)
KV-hit-rate 0.78 -> 0.54
avg_batch_tokens 230 -> 410
cpu-sched-queue-time +12ms median
```

Kevin: token_silo sounds promising. Two quick notes: (1) prefer softcap + reserve slots over hard cap so we don't regress throughput for heavy bursty traffic; (2) we should simulate per-card slot reservation (e.g., reserve 1-3 micro-slots per card for large requests) to avoid starving short requests. I can run a micro-sim with your numbers and a conservative reserve of 2 slots per A100.

Olivia: draft runtime config patch i mocked for the console / serving runtime:
```yaml
batching:
  accelerator_profiles:
    a100:
      soft_max_tokens: 48000
      reserve_slots: 2
    h100:
      soft_max_tokens: 64000
      reserve_slots: 1
    a10:
      soft_max_tokens: 18000
      reserve_slots: 1
    l4:
      soft_max_tokens: 10000
      reserve_slots: 1
    t4:
      soft_max_tokens: 6000
      reserve_slots: 1
  policy:
    large_request_routing: token_silo
    fallback_behavior: prefer_kernel_stability
```
This wires into the kernel selector to bias packing that places long requests into reserved slots.

Sam: nice. We need an experiment plan + clear metrics to judge success: p95 latency, KV-hit-rate, kernel-fallback-rate, aggregate throughput. Success target: fallback uplift <5% (ideally negative) and p95 <= baseline +10%. Can we run a 6h canary at 10% traffic in eu-west?

Maria: i'll spin the canary today. plan: 10% traffic eu-west, mixed-production trace replay for 6h, collect: p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, kernel-fallbacks, per-model throughput. i'll post dashboards.

Kevin: also add a feature flag `--enable-token-silo` and a tracing tag `token_silo=true` so we can roll forward/back easily and filter traces. i'll run the sim first and share expected delta.

Olivia: i'll open the PR with the config + runtime toggle + unit tests for the allocator. rollout notes in PR description.

Sam: owners: @Maria run canary, @Kevin sim + perf-model, @Olivia PR + ops docs. add a runbook link for rollback: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/token-siloing

deploy-bot: canary deploy started on eu-west with 10% traffic — build #2891

Maria: quick first-hour update from canary: mixed-workload p95 improved ~12%, KV-hit-rate +6%, kernel-fallback-rate -0.9%. throughput steady. i'll let it run and post full 6h graphs.

Kevin: simulation results looked similar — reserve_slots=2 on A100 + soft_max 48k gives the best tradeoff in our model (throughput -0.6%, p95 -8% for mixed workload).

Olivia: opened PR #4127 with config + toggle + rollout steps. tagged @Sam @Maria @Kevin. PTAL. :thumbsup:

Sam: thanks — if the 6h confirms, we'll bake defaults into the next runtime release and add a telemetry alarm for token_silo toggles.

Maria: continuing run. will post final numbers and cutoff criteria in ~5h.
